summary: Tested the CloudIVR AI agent 'First message' / 'Wait for hello' / opening preview / script guide work. Backend pytest 13/13 passed (CRUD of firstMessage+waitForHello, defaults, no screening/review fields, opening-preview cases a-h, auth required, AI campaign 201 DRY RUN). Node unit tests 13/13 passed (fill/stripNotes/openingInfo/prepare, instructions() has '# How the call started' with exact opening + 'never greet or introduce yourself again', goal has [PAUSE] removed and [Client Full Name]/[First Name] -> Alex, no 'screen' module). text-triggers.js, bulk-call-service.js, campaign-live.js, ai-agent/* load cleanly. Live OpenAI Realtime test talks (3 short runs, ~55 s total): waitForHello:false -> opening spoken first, the next turn did not greet or introduce again; waitForHello:true + 6 s silence -> agent silent, then opening once after ~4 s ('[AIAgent] opening after no hello' logged); waitForHello:true + short 1.2 s 'Hi...' at 0.5 s -> 'opening after hello' logged, opening once. Frontend: the new form fields, toggle, live preview (updates about 1 s after typing, record toggle adds and removes 'This call may be recorded.'), no-name line, added-note, 5 guide tips + example, save + reload keeps both values, Test talk outbound note depends on waitForHello, FR/ES labels translated while the preview sentences stay in English (data-no-translate). No 'In review'/'Blocked'/'safety review' text on the agents list, agent form, campaign new (AI picker) or campaign detail.

minor.issue: The 4 s hello fallback timer is not paused when the person starts talking (input_audio_buffer.speech_started). If the lead starts speaking before 4 s and is still talking at 4 s, the agent starts the opening over them. Reproduced: caller audio of 4.85 s starting at 0.5 s -> log shows 'opening after no hello' while the caller was still speaking. Fix: in case 'input_audio_buffer.speech_started', if (this.waitHello && !this.opened) clearTimeout(this.helloTimer) (and optionally set a longer safety timer), so speech_stopped opens the call.

In one waitForHello run the second agent turn began 'Hi, Alex. Thank you for asking...'. This is a short greeting back after the caller said 'Hi', not a second self-introduction. In another run, with empty FAQs, the model said 'We are open on Saturdays', which is an invented fact (older model-compliance issue, not caused by this change).

integration_issues.issue: ai-test-outbound-note reads the saved agent.waitForHello, so it shows the wrong text after the toggle is changed but not saved yet. Minor.

issues: The translated example first message drops the fallback syntax: FR 'Bonjour {lead_name}, ici {name}...' and ES 'Hola {lead_name}, soy {name}...', while the English is 'Hi {lead_name|there}, ...'. Keep a fallback, e.g. {lead_name|à vous} / {lead_name|qué tal}, or at least {lead_name|...}, in fr.json/es.json key 'Example first message: ...'.

action_items: bridge.js: clear or extend helloTimer on input_audio_buffer.speech_started while waiting for hello, so the agent never opens over a lead who is talking
fr.json/es.json: keep the {lead_name|fallback} form in the translated script-guide example
Optional: make the TestTalk outbound note follow the unsaved waitForHello value, or say 'save to apply'
critical_code_review_comments: bridge.js helloTimer only opens the call on speech_stopped or after 4 s. There is no handling of speech_started, which causes the overlap described above.

opening-preview: the inbound preview of a lead-oriented first message turns into 'May I speak with the right person?'. That is correct by design but reads oddly for inbound calls. Consider a hint that {lead_name} is empty on inbound calls.

success_rate.backend: 100% (26/26 automated), live WS 3/3 with 1 timing edge case
success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested checks (1 minor i18n content issue)
